title: Sandisk Stock (SNDK) Falls 1.5% After Druckenmiller Exit (Nov 17)
summary: Sandisk (SNDK) fell 1.47% to $797.24 on Nov 17 as GuruFocus tied the drop to Druckenmiller's exit and GF Securities warned of NAND oversupply.
body_markdown:
Chip peers fell by smaller margins.[Micron (MU)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mu/) declined 0.92% to $712.42 and[Nvidia (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) slipped 0.44% to $155.46, as Nvidia fell ahead of its[third-quarter results](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/nvidia-first-report-without-huang-tonight/) scheduled after the closing bell, per[Barron's](https://finance.yahoo.com/m/5d4c8ff4-57bc-3350-b217-681441a4f8b3/nvidia%2C-intel%2C-salesforce%2C.html) . Sandisk now sits 66.14% below its 52-week high of $2,354.39 and 335.65% above its 52-week low of $183.00.


## Why Sandisk Stock Fell


According to[GuruFocus](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/sandisk-stocks-fall-5-43-180327218.html) , the morning drop followed a disclosure that Duquesne Family Office, run by Stanley Druckenmiller, had sold its entire Sandisk position. Duquesne held 34,900 shares worth about $79.4 million at June 30 and none at September 30, GuruFocus reported.


The same day, as reported by[GuruFocus](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/micron-sandisk-sk-hynix-face-174959688.html) , GF Securities warned that weaker demand and expanding production could leave NAND flash memory in oversupply in 2027. The firm now expects NAND prices to be flat in the first quarter of 2027 and to decline over the following three quarters, after earlier forecasting growth of 6% and 3% in the first two quarters.


The move extends a longer slide. According to[TipRanks](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/could-not-says-investor-sandisk-215607193.html) , the shares fell again after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive on November 12, and per the[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/why-sandisk-stock-keeps-going-184255118.html) , Sandisk was down 32% in November as of Tuesday. Its author argued that data centers buy Nvidia's AI chips and Sandisk's NAND in pairs, so weaker Nvidia demand could weigh on Sandisk.


## SNDK Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- According to the company's[fiscal first-quarter 2027 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002023554/000162828026068243/sndkq1-27ex991xpressrelease.htm) , revenue rose 23% from the prior quarter and 378% from a year earlier to $11.03 billion, while data center revenue grew 61% sequentially to $4.80 billion.
- Sandisk guided fiscal second-quarter revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion, per the same release.
- TipRanks reported remaining performance obligations of $88.9 billion, mostly from multiyear supply deals covering about half of fiscal 2027 bits and two-thirds of fiscal 2028 bits.


### Risks


- GF Securities expects NAND supply to grow 21% in 2026, 28% in 2027 and 30% in 2028, and the GuruFocus report said Sandisk's focus on NAND means more profit volatility.
- Citing SemiAnalysis, the Motley Fool author wrote that AI chip capital spending could come in 19% below previous estimates in 2027 and 28% below in 2028.
- TipRanks noted that Sandisk relies on its Kioxia venture for almost all of its wafers, sells to a fairly concentrated group of large buyers and saw consumer revenue fall 29% sequentially.


Next on the calendar, the company's release states that holders of record on November 9 receive seven additional shares for each share held after the close on Thursday, November 19, with split-adjusted trading expected to begin at the open on Friday, November 20.
